sets.setting: at a relative's house during a family gathering

speakers.M: her cousin, a boy of about the same age

sets.title: The flashlight hunt before dinner
sets.transcript:
M: There you are. Grandma wants us to keep Alfie and Birdie busy until dinner. She says they've knocked over the umbrella stand twice already.
W: Yeah, I heard the crash. Dinner's at eight, so that's about forty minutes. How about a treasure hunt in the back garden, with flashlights? It's nearly dark, and they'd love that.
M: In the garden? It rained all afternoon. The grass is basically mud, and your mum's only just finished mopping the hall.
W: We'd stick to the stone path and the patio. Nobody has to step on the grass. And the path's got those little solar lamps along the edge, so they'll see where they're going.
M: The path will still be soaking, though.
W: Not really. It's stone, so it dries fast. It was dry when I came round the back.
M: Hmm. I was going to say we put a film on upstairs. Our grandpa's got that huge screen in the back bedroom, and they'd actually sit still for once.
W: Sitting still isn't what they need, though. They had films on the whole drive here.
M: Wait, I thought they came on the train with your dad.
W: Dad's coming tomorrow. I only got here twenty minutes ago, and Birdie kicked the back of my seat the entire way, and her brother sang the whole time. Trust me, they need to run around.
M: Fair enough. But what if they get bored after one clue?
W: They won't. I'll write eight short clues, and each one leads to the next. The last one's under the big flower pot by the back door, with a bag of toffees.
M: Should I ask if dinner can wait a bit, just in case?
W: No need. Forty minutes is plenty for eight clues.
M: OK, the hunt it is. What do you want me to do?
W: I'll write the clues at the kitchen table. Can you go and round up Alfie and Birdie? I think they've climbed up to the attic again.
M: On it. I'll go and grab them now.
